subject: Economics
description: Fiscal deficit, GDP, direct vs indirect taxes, Finance Commission

questions.stem: The UNION BUDGET of India is presented in Parliament under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 112 — Annual Financial Statement — the constitutional term for the Union Budget. Article 110 defines a Money Bill. Article 280 sets up the Finance Commission. Article 352 deals with National Emergency.
questions.subject: Economics

options.option_text: Total government expenditure minus total revenue (excluding borrowings)

questions.explanation: Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure − (Revenue + non-debt Capital receipts). It is the government's TOTAL borrowing requirement. Revenue deficit = revenue expenditure − revenue receipts. Primary deficit = Fiscal deficit − interest payments.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: Which of the following is a DIRECT TAX?
questions.explanation: Direct tax — burden cannot be shifted; paid directly by the person/entity (Income Tax, Corporate Tax, Capital Gains Tax, Wealth Tax [abolished]). Indirect tax — burden shifted to consumer (GST, customs, excise).
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: GDP at MARKET PRICES equals GDP at FACTOR COST plus:
questions.explanation: GDP_MP = GDP_FC + Net Indirect Taxes. Market prices include indirect taxes paid and exclude subsidies received. Factor cost is the pure return to factors of production. (NNP = GDP − Depreciation. GNP = GDP + NFIA.)
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The FINANCE COMMISSION of India is constituted every:
questions.explanation: Article 280 — the President constitutes a Finance Commission every 5 years (or earlier if necessary). It recommends the devolution of taxes between the Union and the States. The 15th FC (Chair: N. K. Singh) covered FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26. The 16th FC is now in operation.
questions.subject: Economics

options.option_text: Impose a ceiling on fiscal and revenue deficits to enforce fiscal discipline

questions.explanation: Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003 — aimed at cutting the fiscal deficit to 3% of GDP and eliminating the revenue deficit. Targets have been revised repeatedly (e.g., through amendments during covid-era slippages). N. K. Singh Committee (2017) recommended a debt-to-GDP anchor.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: If GDP growth rate is 7% and inflation is 5%, the NOMINAL GDP growth rate is (approximately):
questions.explanation: Nominal GDP growth ≈ Real GDP growth + Inflation = 7 + 5 = 12% (approximately, for small rates). The reverse: Real = Nominal − Inflation. This is the Fisher approximation.
